key_insight: LLM judges can match clinicians well on safety and factual checks in patient communication, but they are less reliable for judging communication quality.
clinical_relevance: This could enable scalable oversight of AI-generated patient-facing content, especially for high-stakes materials like informed consent, while highlighting the need for human-centered calibration.
method: Built a stakeholder-informed 7-criterion rubric covering safety, reliability, and communication quality.
Validated the rubric on the ICON-Bench informed-consent benchmark.
Benchmarked 19 LLM judges against clinician and patient-advocate ratings.
evidence_signal: Clinician ratings showed strong interrater reliability, and LLM judges achieved strong clinician agreement for safety screening and factual verification (Spearman rho > 0.80) but weaker agreement for communication quality (rho < 0.60).
watch_item: Patient advocates rated communication quality lower than clinicians and LLM judges, suggesting current judge systems may miss patient-centered concerns.
paper_title: Validating LLM judges for automated oversight of patient communication
